info.bio: Ella Maria Lani Yelich-O'Connor (Devonport, Auckland, Nueva Zelanda, 7 de noviembre de 1996), más conocida por su nombre artístico Lorde, es una cantautora neozelandesa. A los 12 años de edad, firmó un contrato con la discográfica Universal Music, gracias a Scott Maclachlan, su futuro mánager. Poco tiempo después, empezó a componer sus propias canciones, y se alió con Joel Little, quien las produjo. Lorde publicó su EP debut, The Love Club, en noviembre de 2012, de forma gratuita en Soundcloud.

podcast.title: Early Career and SoundCloud (2012)
podcast.body: Originally a teenage indie musician from New Zealand, Lorde began releasing songs on SoundCloud in 2012. "Then there was Lord, originally a teenage indie musician of New Zealand who began dropping songs on SoundCloud in 2012."

podcast.title: Target of Charli XCX's "Girl So Confusing" (2024)
podcast.body: New Zealand pop star Lorde was correctly identified by fans as the target of Charli XCX's 2024 apparent diss track "Girl So Confusing." The song described a female pop star who "kind of looked like her, with similar curly hair," and with whom Charli had "seemingly fallen out," setting the stage for a unique resolution. "fans correctly guessed that Charlie's target on the song was New Zealand pop star, Lord."

podcast.title: Age Conspiracy Theory
podcast.body: Upon the release of *Pure Heroine* in 2013, some believed Lorde, then 16, was actually 45 years old, arguing that her music's maturity could only come from an "old soul." This theory was fueled by alleged old interviews where she supposedly preferred the name "Ella" and stated her age as 45. The TV show *South Park* even incorporated this theory into a story arc, portraying Lorde as a 45-year-old geologist named Randy Marsh. "The people who believe in this theory point to some old interviews allegedly given by Lord, where she says she prefers to go by the name of Ella and that she's actually 45 years old."

podcast.title: Convergence of Female Artists
podcast.body: Lorde is mentioned as one of several contemporary female artists who, along with Florence + The Machine, Sia, Adele, Lady Gaga, and Lana Del Rey, are perceived to be converging stylistically due to their reliance on the same professional lyricists and producers. "están los letristas que trabajan con sí, a los que trabajan con Adele, con Lord, con Lady Gaga."

podcast.title: Cosmopolitan's Ranking
podcast.body: Cosmopolitan magazine, known for content on makeup and other lifestyle topics, also published its list for the best album of the year, selecting Lorde's "Melodrama". While the album is acknowledged as great, the speaker found the reasoning behind Cosmopolitan's ranking of the top 20 or 25 albums to be amusing, suggesting that the person compiling the list might not have even listened to the albums, especially past September. "el más divertido de Cosmo Politan, yo creo que es leerse los razonamientos, que han puesto para hacer su ranking."

podcast.title: Critical Reception - Quality Evolution
podcast.body: Despite some initial skepticism from critics due to Lorde's low activity in the years following her debut, *Melodrama* showcased a significant leap in quality, surprising everyone. "Lord yo creo que ha llegado a otros niveles de calidad que nos han dejado todos sorprendidos."

podcast.title: Cultural Impact and Satirical Recognition
podcast.body: Lorde's immense popularity and influence were underscored when the TV show *South Park* created an elaborate backstory about her actually being a male geologist from Colorado who uses auto-tune, a clear sign of her widespread cultural recognition. "And you know that you've made it when South Park has a whole backstory about her actually being a male geologist from Colorado working with auto-tune."

podcast.title: Early Breakthrough and Critical Acclaim
podcast.body: Lorde emerged as a young artist who quickly garnered significant attention due to her distinctiveness. Upon the release of her debut album, *Pure Heroine*, at age 16, she was lauded with phrases like "pop prodigy," "voice of a generation," "spokesman for a female rock resurgence," and "new queen of alternative," signifying her profound impact. "Frees is like pop-a-protigy and voice of a generation started being thrown around. Let me give you a few more. Spokesman for a female rock resurgence, the new queen of alternative."

podcast.title: Philanthropic and Social Responsibility
podcast.body: Lorde has actively engaged in social responsibility, assisting victims of a typhoon in the Philippines and contributing funds to an organization dedicated to raising awareness of Batten disease, a fatal neurodegenerative disorder. She also raised money for the Free Tibet movement and has made various other contributions to health causes, particularly in her home country of New Zealand. "Lord has helped out victims of a typhoon in the Philippines. She's contributed funds to an organization that raises awareness of a fatal neurodegenerative disorder called Baton disease. She's raised money for the free Tibet movement and she's made other contributions to various health causes, especially at home in New Zealand."

podcast.title: Streaming Success with Pop-Leaning Rock Sound
podcast.body: Lorde is cited as an artist whose songs achieved hundreds of millions, and sometimes billions, of streams throughout the 2010s. Her sound was characterized as leaning towards the pop end of rock, indicating a successful adaptation to the changing music consumption landscape. "There was the luminaires, Lorde, Imagine Dragons, Coldplay, Mumford and Sons. They all had songs that streamed hundreds of millions, and in some cases billions of times through the decade."

xref.title: Juno Awards 50th Anniversary Performance
xref.body: The surviving members of The Tragically Hip reunited to perform at the 50th anniversary of the Juno Awards on June 6th, 2021, with Feist filling in on vocals. There was initial "resistance amongst all of us to delve back in and open that door," but the decision was made due to the significance of the 50th anniversary, the honor being received, and the desire to support musicians and live venues during a period of hardship. Feist was suggested as a singer, and the band felt "everyone had that same response," believing Gordon Downie would approve. The performance was compared to Nirvana's Rock and Roll Hall of Fame induction performance with female vocalists like Lorde, St. Vincent, Kim Gordon, and Joan Jett. "if there was a time when we were going to entertain the idea that this is probably it."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Ongoing Criticism and Immense Influence
xref.body: Despite her charitable work and evolving social views, Lana Del Rey remains subject to criticism, primarily regarding the themes and imagery present in her music. Nevertheless, her influence on contemporary artists such as Billie Eilish, Lorde, and Halsey is considered immense. "Even with all that, Lana is subject to all sorts of criticism, mostly over the themes and imagery in her music. At the same time, though, her influence has been immense. Could there have been a Billie Eilish or Lord or Halsey without Lana Del Rey? I'd say no."

xref.body: Grace Jones exerted a significant influence on a diverse range of artists, including Annie Lennox of Eurythmics, Madonna, Lady Gaga, Rihanna, and Lorde. Her impact extends to the drag queen and cross-dressing scene, solidifying her status as a powerful and transformative figure.
